Title: Self-Organized Variational Autoencoders for Learned Image Compression
Text:
SELF-ORGANIZED VARIATIONAL AUTOENCODERS (SELF-VAE)
FOR LEARNED IMAGE COMPRESSION
M. Akın Yılmaz1, Onur Keles¸1, Hilal G¨uven1, A. Murat Tekalp1, Junaid Malik2, Serkan Kıranyaz3
1Dept. of Electrical & Electronics Eng., Koc¸ University, 34450 ˙Istanbul, Turkey
2Tampere University, Tampere, Finland
3Qatar University, Doha, Qatar
ABSTRACT
In end-to-end optimized learned image compression, it is
standard practice to use a convolutional variational autoen-
coder with generalized divisive normalization (GDN) to
transform images into a latent space. Recently, Operational
Neural Networks (ONNs) that learn the best non-linearity
from a set of alternatives, and their “self-organized” variants,
Self-ONNs, that approximate any non-linearity via Taylor
series have been proposed to address the limitations of con-
volutional layers and a ﬁxed nonlinear activation.
In this
paper, we propose to replace the convolutional and GDN
layers in the variational autoencoder with self-organized
operational layers, and propose a novel self-organized varia-
tional autoencoder (Self-VAE) architecture that beneﬁts from
stronger non-linearity. The experimental results demonstrate
that the proposed Self-VAE yields improvements in both
rate-distortion performance and perceptual image quality.
Index Terms— end-to-end learned image compression,
variational autoencoder, self-organized operational layer,
rate-distortion performance, perceptual quality metrics
1. INTRODUCTION
End-to-end optimization of rate-distortion (RD) performance
using nonlinear transforms via a variational autoencoder with
generalized divisive normalization (GDN) nonlinearity [1]
was ﬁrst proposed in [2, 3] and [4].
In recent years, im-
provements in the learned entropy models that is an integral
part of this framework enabled learned image compression
methods [5–9] to outperform standard image compression
methods such as JPEG [10], JPEG2000 [11], and BPG [12].
Independent from recent developments in learned image
compression, Operational Neural Networks (ONNs) [13–18]
that are heterogeneous networks with nonlinear nodal opera-
tors, and their “self-organized” variants, Self-ONNs [19,20],
with a novel generative neuron model that can approximate

In this paper, based on these recent works, we propose a
self-organized variational autoencoder (Self-VAE) by replac-
ing the convolutional and GDN layers in the generic varia-
tional autoencoder with the operational layers of Self-ONNs
in order to beneﬁt from stronger non-linearity. The rest of
the paper is organized as follows: Section 2 discusses related
works and our contributions. The proposed self-organized
variational autoencoder architecture is introduced in Sec-
tion 3.
Section 4 presents experimental results for image
compression. Finally, Section 5 concludes the paper.
2. RELATED WORK AND CONTRIBUTIONS
2.1. Image Compression
The state of the art in image compression by nonlinear trans-
form coding is summarized in [21]. The improvements over
arXiv:2105.12107v3  [eess.IV]  28 May 2021


time were achieved by better entropy modeling. In [5–9], en-
tropy models with different complexity were used to model
the distribution of latent variables to achieve better compres-
sion performance. In [5, 6], the latent distribution is mod-
elled by a Gaussian, whose mean and/or scale are estimated
by an additional hyperprior network. In [6], this is combined
with an autoregressive model to jointly optimize latent distri-
bution parameters. In [8], a Gaussian mixture model is used
as a more ﬂexible entropy model and attention modules are
added to minimize the distortion between original and recon-
structed images. Sequential channel-conditional slices and la-
tent residual prediction are proposed in [9].
In all these works, GDN layers, which are expected to pro-
vide Gaussian latent variables [1], are the only source of non-
linearity in the variational autoencoder to achieve nonlinear
transform coding. In this work, we replace convolutional and
GDN layers with self-organized operational layers to achieve
stronger nonlinearity and better performance.
2.2. Self-ONNs
ONNs based on Generalized Operational Perceptrons [13–
18], and their self-organized variants, Self-ONNs [19, 20],
based on the generative neuron model (see Section 3.1) have
recently been proposed as heterogeneous network models that
are capable of performing any non-linear kernel transforma-
tion. While conventional ONNs have to search for the best
kernel operators from a pre-determined operator set library,
Self-ONNs can generate the kernel operator by a Taylor series
approximation of the desired order. It has been noted that ex-
haustive search for the best transformation makes ONNs com-
putationally expensive [13, 19, 22]; hence, Self-ONNs have
become a more promising and efﬁcient network architecture
that can provide an utmost level of diversity. In this work, we
extend Self-ONNs to Self-VAEs in order to use them for end-
to-end RD-optimized nonlinear transform image compression
for the ﬁrst time.
2.3. Contributions
The main contributions of this paper are:
• We propose a novel self-organized variational autoen-
coder (Self-VAE) architecture by replacing the convo-
lutional and GDN layers in a convolutional VAE with
self-organized operational layers (SOL) in Section 3
• We employ the Self-VAE as encoder and decoder net-
works in the nonlinear transform coding paradigm [6],
beneﬁting from the ability of SOLs to learn highly com-
plex functions [19] in Section 4.

A generative neuron with 3 × 3 kernels, a = 0 and q = 3
is illustrated in Figure 2. Each neuron takes a tensor as input
and outputs a single channel. The outputs must be limited
within a small range around a before they are input to the next
generative neuron, which will also perform a Taylor series
expansion around a. Setting a = 0, the activation can be
taken as tanh(x) to bound the outputs in the range [−1 1].
Note that if we choose q = 1 and a = 0, the generative neuron
reduces to the classic convolutional neuron.
A SOL is formed by cout generative neurons. For a cin-
channel input tensor, a SOL is composed of cout banks of
q-branch ﬁlterbanks, where each ﬁlterbank represents a gen-
erative neuron, depicted in Figure 2, with the parameters wn,
n = 1, 2, . . . , q denoting cin-channel convolution kernels and
w0 is a bias term. These parameters can be learned during
training using the back-propagation algorithm.
3.2. Self-Organized Variational AutoEncoder (Self-VAE)
While any convolutional VAE can be converted into a Self-
VAE, in this work, we have taken the VAE architecture in [6]
as the baseline model. We replace convolution layers fol-
lowed by GDN activations in the encoder and decoder by SOL

4. EVALUATION
We evaluate the performance of the Self-VAE in the image
compression task. The details of the training process are dis-
cussed in Section 4.1. Experimental setup and results are pre-
sented in Section 4.2 and 4.3, respectively.
4.1. Training Details
We train our self-VAE image compression network, where
each SOL has c = 192 channels, on the Vimeo-90k dataset [23].
In order to construct the RD curve, we trained the network
for four different λ = 0.012, 0.026, 0.042, 0.056.
During
training, we apply 256 × 256 random cropping for data aug-
mentation. The mini-batch size is set to 16 and optimization
is performed for 1M steps. Adam optimizer [24] is used for
the training process. The initial learning rate is set to 1e-4
and dropped to 1e-5 at 500K steps. We also apply gradient
clipping on the norm of the gradients with maximum norm
value is set to 1.
4.2. Experimental Setup
We evaluate the performance of Self-VAE on the commonly
used Kodak images, which consists of 24 uncompressed im-
ages. To evaluate the rate-distortion performance we used

those of GDN-based codec [6] and benchmark BPG codec.

regions on the curve, Self-VAE network gives superior results
compared to [6]. BD-rate [25] improvements provided by the
proposed codec over [6] and BPG are presented in Figure 5.

The LPIPS scores [26] (lower is better) tabulated in Ta-
ble 1 veriﬁes that the perceptual quality of images generated
by the Self-VAE codec is superior to those of GDN-based
codec [6] and BPG.
In terms of model complexity, the Self-VAE model has
q = 3 times more learnable parameters. However, this does
not affect the inference time since q convolutions in each gen-
erative neuron are performed in parallel.
5. CONCLUSION
We propose a novel Self-VAE network based on SOLs that
are composed of generative neurons to replace VAE architec-
tures that are based on convolutional neurons. Experimental
results demonstrate that when widely used convolution and
GDN layers in the state-of-the-art learned image codecs are
replaced by SOL, the RD performance and visual quality im-
proves signiﬁcantly compared to their anchor models using
the same entropy/context model. Since the proposed SOL is
a versatile network layer, it can be directly plugged into any
learned image codec to achieve superior performance.

In this paper, we propose to replace the convolutional and GDN layers in the variational autoencoder with self-organized operational layers, and propose a novel self-organized varia- tional autoencoder (Self-VAE) architecture that beneﬁts from stronger non-linearity. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Self-VAE yields improvements in both rate-distortion performance and perceptual image quality.
